# Parser fixtures

Provenance matters here: a parser tested only against files you wrote yourself will
pass while failing on real reports, because hand-written fixtures encode the same
assumptions as the parser. Every fixture below is genuine tool output.

## Real output, captured from existing suites

| File | Producer | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `junit/newman-restful-booker.xml` | Newman (Postman CLI) | Trimmed to the first 5 suites. All passing — the "nothing failed" path. No `file` attribute on any testcase, which is typical and forces `test_id` to degrade gracefully. |
| `allure/playwright-producer/` | allure-playwright | One result per status, including `broken`. The `failed` result carries screenshot/video/trace attachments **nested inside steps**, not at the top level. |
| `allure/pytest-producer/` | allure-pytest | Same format, different `fullName` grammar (`pkg.Module.Class#test` vs Playwright's `path.spec.ts:line:col`). |

## Generated by running a purpose-built suite

Written to cover statuses the captured reports do not contain. Still real reporter
output — a throwaway suite was executed and its reports kept verbatim.

| File | Producer | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `junit/pytest-suite.xml` | pytest `--junitxml` | pass, fail, skip, error, parametrised names, class-scoped tests |
| `pytest/pytest-report.json` | pytest-json-report | same suite, setup/call/teardown phase durations |
| `playwright/playwright-report.json` | Playwright `json` reporter | `timedOut` status, a genuine retry sequence that fails then passes, and one that fails all three attempts |

## Scrubbing

Hostnames replaced with `ci-runner-01`; absolute paths rewritten to `/repo` or
`/home/runner`. Nothing from `blue-ribbon-qa-automation` is used here — that is
employer data and does not belong in a public repository.
